findings.summary: Larchmont-GNN outperforms Quintrell-MP on average test ROC-AUC across the six scaffold-split datasets (79.4 vs 78.4), and achieves higher ROC-AUC on five of the six datasets (Gorseway-Perm, Hollin-Sol, Ivybridge-Tox, Jessamine-Kin, Kelso-Brain), with a tie on Lumley-Metab (69.8 vs 69.5).
findings.scope: Six scaffold-split datasets, test ROC-AUC (×100), mean over 5 seeds
findings.caveats: No statistical tests reported; differences are small (0.1–1.6 points) and may not be significant.

findings.summary: Larchmont-GNN does not outperform Avonlea-Chem-XL, a much larger pretrained model, on average test ROC-AUC (79.4 vs 80.0) and is lower on five of six datasets (all except Hollin-Sol, where it is 84.1 vs 83.5).
findings.scope: Six scaffold-split datasets, test ROC-AUC (×100), mean over 5 seeds
findings.caveats: Avonlea-Chem-XL is a reference model with 310M parameters and 2400 GPU-hours pretraining cost; no statistical tests reported.

findings.summary: Ablation shows each Larchmont-GNN component contributes to performance: removing ring-aware pooling lowers average ROC-AUC from 79.4 to 78.7, removing distance features lowers it to 78.9, and removing both lowers it to 78.0.
findings.scope: Average test ROC-AUC (×100) over six datasets, mean over 5 seeds
findings.caveats: No statistical tests reported; differences are small (0.5–1.4 points).

findings.summary: Larchmont-GNN has 4.8M parameters and 210 ms inference time per 1,000 molecules, slightly larger and slower than Quintrell-MP (4.1M, 180 ms) but far smaller and faster than Avonlea-Chem-XL (310M, 2950 ms); Larchmont-GNN and Quintrell-MP require no pretraining cost, while Avonlea-Chem-XL requires 2400 GPU-hours.
findings.scope: Model size (M parameters), inference time (ms per 1,000 molecules), pretraining cost (GPU-hours)
findings.caveats: Inference time and parameters are single reported values, not averaged over seeds.

sentences.text: Across the six scaffold-split datasets, Larchmont-GNN achieved a higher average test ROC-AUC than Quintrell-MP (79.4 vs 78.4) and outperformed it on five of the six datasets, with a small margin on Lumley-Metab (69.8 vs 69.5).

However, Larchmont-GNN did not surpass the much larger pretrained reference model Avonlea-Chem-XL, which achieved a higher average ROC-AUC (80.0 vs 79.4) and was higher on five of six datasets, except Hollin-Sol (84.1 vs 83.5).

Ablation results indicate that both components contribute to Larchmont-GNN's performance: removing ring-aware pooling reduced average ROC-AUC from 79.4 to 78.7, removing distance features to 78.9, and removing both to 78.0.

Larchmont-GNN (4.8M parameters, 210 ms per 1,000 molecules) is slightly larger and slower than Quintrell-MP (4.1M, 180 ms) but far more efficient than Avonlea-Chem-XL (310M, 2950 ms), and unlike the pretrained model, it requires no pretraining cost.
